Work in /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (a Lean 4 + Mathlib project; mathlib source is at /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/ — a SHARED package dir at the workspace root, NOT under the project).

THE CLAIM: the file AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange.lean closes the campaign gate `Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` (declared at AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforward.lean:373) with a genuine, non-vacuous, sorry-free instance `AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve`.

YOUR LENS: **vacuity and hidden triviality.** Do not audit proof steps for correctness; hunt for ways the result could be TRUE BUT EMPTY. Concretely:

(a) The instance's hypotheses are `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]` for `C : CategoryTheory.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))`, `k` a field. Find out whether ANY concrete object in this workspace or in mathlib satisfies all three simultaneously. Try to actually construct one in a scratch Lean file — e.g. `Adelic.p1Over k` (defined somewhere in AlgebraicJacobian/, grep for `def p1Over`), or a curve from `references/challenge.lean` at the workspace root. Compile the attempt with `lake env lean /tmp/probe.lean` from the project directory. If you CANNOT exhibit one and cannot find one, say so loudly — that is the strongest possible refutation.

(b) The proof internally uses `[HasFiniteMapToP1 C]`. Determine whether that class has a real producer reachable from the three hypotheses above, or whether it is itself an unproduced gate. Find the instance declaration and check what IT depends on. (A memory note in this workspace claims HasFiniteMapToP1's own docstring says it "carries no instance" but that this is stale and it does synthesize — verify which is true TODAY, by compiling `example (C : ...) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : HasFiniteMapToP1 C := inferInstance`.)

(c) Look for statements in the dependency chain that are TRUE FOR THE WRONG REASON — a `Prop` definition that is trivially satisfiable, an existential over an unconstrained object, a hypothesis that is never used, or a conclusion that holds vacuously because some indexing set is empty. Pay particular attention to `Adelic.RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange` (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean:429) and `Adelic.exists_gammaBaseChange_of_kerPure` (the new file, §1). Both are existentials of the shape `∃ s, (prescribed values on simple tensors) ∧ Bijective s`. Test whether the prescribed values REALLY pin down `s` uniquely, or whether a degenerate `s` could satisfy them (e.g. if the tensor product were trivial, or if the "prescribed values" constrained nothing because the target module is subsingleton in some case).

(d) There is a recorded historical failure in this project worth re-testing: an earlier "rank leaf" Prop was invented that DROPPED the engine's hypotheses and was outright FALSE (counterexample `A = k[x]`, `M = O/x`), making its consumers vacuously true with clean axioms. Ask of every new `Prop` in the new file: is it true, is it non-vacuous, would a counterexample compile just as happily?

Use `lake env lean` on scratch files in /tmp to test everything you can. `#print axioms`, `#check @name`, and compiling `example ... := inferInstance` are your best tools. Do NOT modify any file in the project.

Report: a verdict REFUTED or NOT-REFUTED for the overall claim, plus the specific evidence. If NOT-REFUTED, state exactly which vacuity checks you actually ran and what they returned — I will not accept "looks fine".

def RigidPushforwardBaseChange (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Prop :=
  ∀ L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules,

    ∀ (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] (φ : A →+* A'),
      IsIso (pushforwardBaseChangeMap
        (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))

class HasRigidPushforward (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : Prop where
  /-- Rank-`χ` local freeness over every finitely generated `k`-algebra. -/

    RigidPushforwardLocallyFree C A
  /-- Arbitrary base change over every finitely generated `k`-algebra. -/

/-- **B3 headline, local-freeness half** (extraction from the gate): for an

pushforward `q_* L` is, near every `t : Spec A`, free of rank

theorem pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing [HasRigidPushforward C]
    (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
    (h1 : ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing L t)
    (t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) :
    ∃ U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens, t ∈ U ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
            (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj L) ≅
        _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
          (ULift.{u} (Fin ((pullback.snd C.hom
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t)))) :=
  HasRigidPushforward.locallyFree A L hL h1 t

10	# `H⁰` commutes with affine base change, in the form the B3 gate consumes
11	
12	`Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean` reduces the second field of the campaign gate
13	`Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` — `Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange` — to the single module-level
14	statement `Adelic.RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange`: bijectivity of the canonical
15	`Γ(Spec A', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Spec A, ⊤)} Γ(C_A, L) → Γ(C_{A'}, g'^* L)`.  This file proves that
16	statement.
17	
18	## §1, the general theorem
19	
20	`exists_gammaBaseChange_of_kerPure` takes a cartesian square
21	
22	```
23	  X' --g'--> X
24	  |f'        |f
25	  v          v
26	  Y' --g---> Y
27	```
28	
29	with `Y`, `Y'` affine and `g'` affine, a bundled 2-affine cover `𝒰` of `X`, a quasi-coherent `M`,
30	and the Čech `H⁰`-purity hypothesis `hker` (the kernel base-change map of the two-term Čech
31	difference `d = 𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase f M` is bijective for every `Γ(Y, ⊤)`-algebra `B`), and
32	produces the canonical comparison
33	
34	`Γ(Y', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(f_* M, ⊤) ≅ Γ(f'_* (g'^* M), ⊤)`, `b ⊗ x ↦ b · baseMap x`.
35	
36	It is a sandwich of three existing pieces: the sheaf condition on both sides
37	(`AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase`, which identifies `Γ` with
38	`ker d`), the affine-base-change Čech square on kernels
39	(`Adelic.exists_kerChartTensorEquiv`, `Picard/RigidPushforwardChartBaseChange.lean`), and the
40	`pushforward`-versus-`baseSections` dictionary at the two tops
41	(`Scheme.Modules.pushforwardTopEquivBaseSections`).  The only computation is that the resulting
42	map does send `b ⊗ x` to `b · baseMap x`, which is the restriction naturality
43	`pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_res'` on each of the two charts.
44	
45	Note what is *not* assumed: `f` is arbitrary — in the application it is the proper, emphatically
46	non-affine family `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A`, which is exactly the case
47	`Picard/RigidPushforwardFrontier.lean` reports as having no infrastructure.
48	
49	Sources: Stacks 01HQ, 02KG at `i = 0`; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5; EGA III 7.7.5.
50	-/

161	/-- **`RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange` is a theorem.**  For the AJC curve `C/k` and every
162	finitely generated `k`-algebra `A`, the formation of `Γ(C_A, L)` for an invertible `L` with
163	fibrewise `h¹ = 0` commutes with every ring map `A → A'`.
164	
165	The Čech `H⁰`-purity fed to §1 is obtained on the 2-affine cover
166	`(p1BaseChangeCoverSquare A).preimage π_A` of `C_A` — the preimage under the finite (hence
167	affine) `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` of the standard 2-chart cover of `ℙ¹_A` — from two inputs:
168	
169	* **surjectivity** of its Čech differential, which is the *first* conjunct of the ℙ¹ engine
170	  `p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing_of_isIntegral` applied to `(π_A)_* L`.  No
171	  transport is needed: `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff_pushforward` is `rfl` and
172	  `moduleSectionDiffBase`'s underlying function *is* `moduleSectionDiff`, so the two
173	  surjectivity statements are the same proposition — in particular the propositional
174	  `q = π_A ≫ p` never has to be crossed;
175	* **flatness** of `Γ(L, U₁ ⊓ U₂)` over `Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`, which is `CoherentSheafFlat q L` read at
176	  the pair `(⊤, U₁ ⊓ U₂)` (`flat_baseSections_of_coherentSheafFlat`) — stated for `q` from the
177	  start, so again no transport.
178	
179	`bijective_kerBaseChange_of_surjective` then gives purity at `q`'s own module structures.  (The
180	alternative recorded in `Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean` — instantiating the engine's
181	*fourth* conjunct instead — avoids the flatness obligation but has to move the whole `letI`
182	dictionary from `p` and the pushforward module to `q` and `L`; flatness is free here, so this
183	route is shorter.)
184	
185	The ℙ¹ engine's `H⁰`-finiteness anchor is `IsIntegral (ℙ¹_k)`
186	(`Adelic.instIsIntegralP1OverLeft`), so the two fields of the gate are not independent — as
187	`Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean`'s dependency warning records. -/
188	theorem rigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange_proved

190	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
191	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] :
192	    RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange C A := by
193	  intro L hL h1 A' _ φ e'
194	  haveI := hL.isFinitePresentation
